findings.original: does not imply the determination of the magnitude of its value
findings.rewrite: does not imply that the magnitude of its value is fixed
findings.problem: "is fixed" can be read as "is constant", turning Marx's point (the equivalent form says nothing about how much value money has) into a claim about whether money's value varies.
findings.fix: does not imply how the magnitude of its value is determined

findings.original: from which it appears that he has not the remotest idea of the real history of the theory
findings.rewrite: which shows that he has not the remotest idea of the real history of the theory
findings.problem: Marx's hedge "it appears" is turned into a flat "shows"; §1.1 says "it appears" stays.
findings.fix: from which it appears that he has not the remotest idea of the real history of the theory

notes_review: The logged calls are sound, including leaving "money form" unglossed in p009 (the §7 wording names gold and would contradict Marx's cattle and slaves) and the literal re-translations in n. 11. "savages" → "tribal peoples" (n. 5) is defensible but ch03-s1 n. 2 keeps "Savages", so the two files now differ; the style bible should settle this one way.
summary: Fidelity is high: all claims, quotations, citations and irony (Roscher, Proudhon, the Apocalypse) survive, with one dropped hedge and one ambiguous "is fixed". Readability is good, with long sentences split cleanly and the §7 explanations placed at the right first uses.
